svg.title: Party wheel — three, two, one, widen then deepen
svg.desc: Comparison E. Progression runs from the outer rim inward: three talents, two follow-ups, one ultimate beside the hero portrait. On a skill every tier-one talent can be bought. Tier two stays open until a follow-up is bought: selecting an owned talent previews its two follow-ups; buying one locks tier two to that talent, and both of its follow-ups can then be bought. The same rule applies from tier two to the ultimate. A skill holds at most six talents. A lock is drawn as a path through a coloured keystone on the line between two tiers; the keystone costs no gem. Class trees stay one choice per tier. Strike is selected with two talents owned and tier two still open. Names and effects are illustrative. Static SVG mockup.
svg.text: COMPARISON E / Buy any talent in a tier. Only one of them carries on to the next tier. Up to six talents per skill.
Square on the rim = skill · Hexagon on the rim = class · Gold ring = owned · Coloured outline = can be bought · Dotted ring = selected or preview · Diamond on a line = lock, costs no gem
Rim → 3 talents → 2 follow-ups of one talent → 1 ultimate of one follow-up, beside the portrait. Icon colour = gem type. Class trees: one choice per tier, the others dim. Centre: unspent gems.
2 of 3 talents owned · no follow-up bought yet
Sweeping strike offers these two follow-ups:
The sweep tears open every enemy it hits.
Each enemy hit by the sweep grants protection.
Leads to the ultimate Unbroken line.
Bulwark sweep can still be bought afterwards.
Arcane strike keeps working; its follow-ups close for good.
Select another owned talent to see its follow-ups instead.
At most six talents on a skill: three, two, one.
STATIC CONCEPT · Names and effects are illustrative.
